label: PV Limiter v1.3
info:
PV Limiter v1.3
=================

Price- and grid-aware power limiter for one or two PV inverters, driven from
Home Assistant. When power is cheap the inverters go to 0% and the flow asks the strategy
arbiter to hold the battery strategy on Charge; when power is expensive they
run at 100% (full output) and the Charge hold is released, so the arbiter puts
back the strategy that was active before; in the normal price band a 5 s loop checks battery state-of-charge
first, then the grid deadband: below 99% SoC it steps the limiter back up
towards 100% (full output), and only at 99% SoC or higher (battery full) does
it step down, and then only while grid power is outside the deadband. PV1 and
PV2 always move in lockstep and are written in parallel. Changing the
thresholds, deadband
or step size while enabled restarts the flow (re-runs the price evaluation).
PV2 is driven only when auto-detected. 3 consecutive bad sensor reads fall
back to a safe 50%. Every inverter write goes through 'Hardware write
guard'; the battery strategy is only changed via 'Strategy arbiter'.

>> Full how-it-works walkthrough - trigger, master gate, every group, the
   required HA helpers and the flow context vars - is in the on-canvas comment
   node titled "📖 Flow Documentation — PV Limiter v1.3 (how it works)". Keep that
   node as the detailed reference; this Info panel holds the summary above and
   the version history below.

Version history
---------------
v1.3 - (21 Oct 2026) Hardening. The battery strategy is no longer written
       here: the cheap band sends a 'hold Charge' request and the high band a
       'release' to 'Strategy arbiter' (link call 'Strategy request').
       The arbiter restores the previous strategy and respects manual
       changes - before, the high band forced 'Dynamic' on every quarter-hour
       price tick. Replaces the input_text.pv_limiter_saved_strategy chain
       of 19 Oct (helper removed). All 10 PV1/PV2 limit writes now go through
       'Hardware write guard' (link call 'Guarded hardware write': clamp
       0-100, skip unchanged, max one write per 4 s per inverter). The log
       line shows what the arbiter did ('strategy: ...'). The HA watchdog
       (packages/nodered_heartbeat.yaml) now sets both limits to 100% when
       the heartbeat is older than 10 min. Version bumped to v1.3.
v1.2 - Curtailment gate tightened and PV1/PV2 stepping made lockstep +
       parallel. Reduction in the normal-price band now requires BOTH the
       normal price band (implicit: the P1 loop only runs there) AND a full
       battery (SoC >= 99%). Below 99% SoC the loop no longer jumps straight
       to 100% but steps the limiter back up by the configured step size, one
       step per 5 s tick. Both inverters are stepped from a single shared base
       (the lower of the two) so they always hold the same limit and a manual
       slider move on one converges back instead of leaving a permanent
       offset, and the PV1/PV2 number.set_value calls are now fired in
       parallel from *Calculate P1 adjustment* instead of chained PV1 -> PV2.
       Step-size clamp in the P1 calc raised from 1-10 to 1-25 so it matches
       the input_number.pv_step_size helper range (values above 10 were
       silently capped before). Flow Documentation node updated to match.
       No new entities or helpers.
v1.1 - Log-noise guard for transient HA dropouts. Added a *Filter transient
       HA drops* function between the tab-wide *Catch all errors* node and
       the logger: bursts of HA WebSocket errors (NoConnectionError /
       Connection lost) are now collapsed to a single log row per 60 s
       window, with a live suppressed-count on the node status, while
       genuine errors still pass through unchanged. New flow context var
       ha_conn_err_window {start,count} holds the rate-limit window. Flow
       Documentation node updated to match. No change to control logic.
v1.0 - Initial release of PV Limiter. Price- and grid-aware power limiter for
       one or two PV inverters: price branches set 0% (cheap, battery Charge)
       or 100% (expensive); the normal-price band runs a 5 s P1 balance loop
       that checks battery SoC first (below 95% drives to 100% to charge, above
       95% trims down only when grid power is outside the deadband) then the
       grid deadband. PV2 is driven only when auto-detected; 3 consecutive bad
       sensor reads fall back to a safe 50%. Changing thresholds, deadband or
       step size while enabled restarts the flow. Starts ENABLED by default
       (On-start inject) and evaluates the price exactly once on deploy.
       Pool-Heat-Pump-style logging: rolling 10-entry buffer published as both
       a JSON entries attribute and a ready-to-render Markdown table, seeded
       with a startup entry on deploy.

info:
# PV Limiter — Flow Documentation (v1.3)

> Version history / change log lives in the tab's **Info** panel (double-click the tab name). This node is the detailed, canonical how-it-works reference.

This flow throttles one or two PV inverters (`number.pv1_power_limit_slider`
and, when detected, `number.pv2_power_limit_slider`, 0–100 %) based on the
**current electricity price** and, in the normal-price band, on **live grid (P1) power** and
**battery state-of-charge (SoC)**. The goal: export nothing (or charge the
battery) when power is cheap, run flat-out when power is expensive, and in the
normal-price band ramp toward full output only while doing so would not push
power onto the grid — curtailing whenever export exceeds the deadband
(regardless of battery SoC), and additionally once the battery is full.

## Big picture

**Trigger:** every change of `sensor.epex_injectie_now` (and once ~15 s
after deploy) runs the decision chain. A separate 5 s timer drives the P1
balance loop. **Master gate:** nothing acts unless `input_boolean.pv_limiter`
is ON.

**PV2 auto-detect:** `sensor.pv_inverters` (state `2`) is cached into flow
var `pv2_present`. Every PV2 write is gated on it and the P1 calc only needs
an PV2 reading when present, so the flow runs on **PV1 alone** when the
second inverter package is not installed.

Three price branches:
- **Low** (price < -(network + federal cost), i.e. below
  `-sensor.epex_afname_extra`) → both PVs to **0 %** + request the
  strategy arbiter to **hold Charge**, loop stopped.
- **High** (price > 0 €/kWh, fixed and strictly positive) → both PVs to
  **100 %** + **release** the Charge hold (the arbiter restores the previous
  strategy), loop stopped.
- **Normal** (negative, but not more negative than the extra cost) → arm the
  **P1 balance loop**, which keeps grid injection at (near) 0.

Watchdog: 3 consecutive bad sensor reads → safe **50 %** fallback.

---

## Groups

**00 Control (enable / disable)** — Manual ▶/⏹ inject buttons and the matching
HA `input_boolean` state listeners. A *Validate & debounce* function (2 s
debounce) rejects bad payloads and toggles `input_boolean.pv_limiter`; the
listener then mirrors the state into flow var `pv_enabled` (disabling also
clears `pv_loop_active`). Every toggle is logged. an *On start:
enable* inject fires once after deploy and turns `input_boolean.pv_limiter`
**ON**, so the flow comes up **enabled by default**.

**01 Price Trigger** — Fires the decision chain. *Price changed* listens to
`sensor.epex_injectie_now`; *Deploy: re-evaluate* injects once 15 s after
deploy and *Read current price* feeds the same entry point so the flow settles
to the right state on restart. A genuine change to any **08 Config Monitoring**
helper (thresholds, deadband, step size) also routes through *Read current
price*, so editing config while the limiter is enabled restarts the decision
chain.

**02 Decision** — The gatekeeper chain: *Flow enabled?* halts unless
`input_boolean.pv_limiter` is ON → *Get extra cost (network+federal)* reads
the dynamic low-threshold source → *Threshold sanity* derives the low
threshold (`-extra_cost`) and validates the numbers against a fixed high
threshold of 0 €/kWh (NaN or low ≥ high routes to the Watchdog) → *Price
branch* switch routes to Low / High (price strictly > 0) / Normal (in
between, price == 0 included). A healthy pass resets `pv_invalid_count`.

**03 Low Price → PV 0 % + Charge** — *Prepare 0 % + stop loop* clears
`pv_loop_active`, sets the desired setpoint to 0/0, then sets both PV
sliders to 0 % and sends *Request: hold Charge* to the strategy arbiter
(link call *Strategy request*). The arbiter only acts on the first request of a
cheap period and leaves a manual strategy change alone. Logged as `cheap_zero`
(with `| strategy: <arbiter result>`).

**04 High Price → PV 100 % + release Charge** — *Prepare 100 % + stop loop*
stops the loop, sets the desired setpoint to 100/100, drives both PV
sliders to 100 % so the inverters run at full output, and sends *Request:
release* to the strategy arbiter: if PV Limiter's Charge hold is still in
force, the arbiter puts back the strategy that was active before it (never a
fixed one); otherwise nothing changes. Logged as `expensive_full` (with
`| strategy: <arbiter result>`).

**05 Normal Price → Activate P1 Loop** — *Activate P1 loop* sets
`pv_loop_active = true`, clears the last-branch marker and nulls `pv_desired`
so the loop re-seeds from the live HA sliders on its next tick. Logged as
`normal_price`.

**06 Watchdog (bad-tick safety fallback)** — A shared bad-tick counter
(`pv_invalid_count`). Bad reads from the Decision chain or the P1 calc land
here; on the **3rd** consecutive strike it forces both PVs to **50 %**, stops
the loop, syncs the setpoint, and resets the counter (a fresh 3 strikes are
needed to fire again). Logged as `watchdog_fallback`.

**07 P1 Balance Loop — every 5 s in the normal-price band** — *Every 5 s* timer
→ *Gate* (runs only when `pv_enabled` and `pv_loop_active` are both true) → reads PV1, PV2, battery SoC and `sensor.p1_meter_power` →
*Calculate P1 adjustment*. The calc trims the PV output up/down by the
configured **step**, checking battery **SoC** first and the grid **deadband**
second. **Priority order: export gate, then battery-full gate, then
deadband:**
- A **race guard** bails if the loop was stopped mid-tick (so it can't
  overwrite a 0/100/50 % write).
- It steps from a flow-maintained **desired setpoint** (`pv_desired`), not by
  reading the slider back each tick (avoids actuator-feedback stalls); a >5 %
  divergence or a stale (>30 s) setpoint re-syncs from the live HA value.
- **Exporting (P1 < -deadband):** already injecting at a negative price —
  step the limiter **down** by one **step** per tick (`reduce`), **regardless
  of battery SoC**.
- **Not exporting, SoC < 99 % (battery not full):** safe to charge — step the
  limiter back **up** towards 100 % by one **step** per tick (`increase`).
- **Not exporting, SoC ≥ 99 % (battery full):** step the limiter **down**
  when grid power is outside the deadband; while |P1| ≤ deadband it holds
  (`balanced`, logged only on transition).
- **Lockstep + parallel:** PV1 and PV2 are always driven to the **same** value.
  Both are stepped from one shared base (the lower of the two, so a manual
  slider move on one inverter converges back instead of leaving a permanent
  offset), and the PV1 and PV2 `number.set_value` calls are fired **in
  parallel** from *Calculate P1 adjustment* rather than chained PV1 → PV2.
- Missing/invalid sensor values → `p1_invalid_input` → Watchdog.

**08 Config Monitoring** — Listeners on `sensor.epex_afname_extra` (the
dynamic low-threshold source), `input_number.pv_step_size`, and
`input_number.pv_p1_deadband`. The high threshold is a fixed constant (0
€/kWh, strictly positive price required) hardcoded in the *Price branch*
switch, not monitored here. *Format config change* caches
each value into flow context (`cfg_*`) so the P1 loop reads config without
polling HA, and logs only genuine changes (the deploy-time emit and no-op
old == new changes are suppressed). Logged as `config_change`. a genuine
change also feeds *01 Price Trigger → Read current price*, so editing the
thresholds, deadband or step size **restarts** the flow (re-runs the price
evaluation) — routed through *Flow enabled?*, so nothing happens while the
limiter is off.

**09 PV2 Detection** — *PV inverters count changed* listens to
`sensor.pv_inverters` (state `2` = PV2 present) (with `outputInitially` so it also fires on
deploy); *Set pv2_present flag* caches the boolean into flow var
`pv2_present` and shows a node status ('PV2 detected' / 'PV1 only'). The
five *PV2 present?* gates and the P1 calc read this flag so PV2 is only
touched when its modbus package exists.

**99 Update UI: PV Limiter log** — Central logger. A *link in* collects events
from every branch; *Build log entry* formats a timestamped entry (icon, level,
group, node, payload), keeps a rolling **10-entry** buffer, and *Set
sensor.pv_limiter_log* writes it to HA — publishing both a JSON `entries`
attribute and a ready-to-render **Markdown table** (`markdown` attribute) for
the dashboard card. An *On deploy: seed log* inject feeds *Build startup event*
so a `startup` entry is written on every deploy, and a tab-wide *Catch all
errors* routes runtime errors into the same logger via *Filter transient HA
drops* — a guard that collapses repeated HA WebSocket dropouts
(`NoConnectionError` / `Connection lost`) into a **single log row per 60 s
window** (showing a live suppressed-count on its node status) while letting
genuine errors pass through untouched, so a brief reconnect no longer spams the
log. The same window also absorbs **entity cache-miss errors** (e.g. `Entity
could not be found in cache for sensor.epex_injectie_now`) that fire when
the read chain runs against an empty entity cache during a reconnect; a
cache-miss on a **healthy** connection (wrong/renamed entity id or a down
integration) is **not** suppressed and still reaches the log.

---

## Writes to equipment and the battery strategy (v1.3)
- **Inverter limits** — every `number.pv1/pv2_power_limit_slider` write is a
  *Guarded: …* function (sets `msg.hw = {entity, value}`) followed by a link
  call to **Guarded hardware write** on tab *Hardware write guard*. The
  guard clamps to 0–100 %, rounds, skips a value the slider already has and
  allows at most one write per 4 s per inverter (a later wish is written when
  the 4 s are over, never dropped). The caller continues with
  `msg.hw_result` = written / unchanged / deferred / rejected.
- **Battery strategy** — never written here. *Request: hold Charge* /
  *Request: release* call **Strategy request** on tab *Strategy arbiter*
  (`msg.arbiter = {requester: 'pv_limiter', action, strategy}`). Priority:
  oscillation guard > PV Limiter > the user's own choice. The arbiter keeps
  its state in `input_text.hbc_strategy_arbiter`.
- Both link calls are **dynamic** (`msg.target` = link-in name), so they keep
  working after an import as a copy. Keep the link-in names unique.

## Required HA helpers
All helpers are defined in the
[`pv_limiter_control.yaml`](https://github.com/coderubbere/HA-PV-Limiter/blob/main/home%20assistant/packages/pv_limiter_control.yaml)
package:
1. `input_boolean.pv_limiter`
2. ~~`input_number.pv_price_threshold_low`~~ — no longer used; the low
   threshold is now derived live from `sensor.epex_afname_extra` (network +
   federal cost per kWh, from `packages/epex_live_sensors.yaml`)
3. ~~`input_number.pv_price_threshold_high`~~ — no longer used; the high
   threshold is now a fixed constant (0 €/kWh) in the *Threshold sanity*
   function
4. `input_number.pv_step_size` (1–25, def 2)
5. `input_number.pv_p1_deadband` (0–500, def 100)

Plus the `sensor.pv_inverters` `command_line` sensor in
`pv_limiter_control.yaml` (state `2` = PV2 present) that drives PV2 auto-detection.

## Key flow context vars
1. `pv_enabled`
2. `pv_loop_active`
3. `pv_desired` {pv1,pv2,ts}
4. `pv_p1_last_branch`
5. `pv_invalid_count`
6. `cfg_step`
7. `cfg_deadband`
8. `cfg_extra_cost_now` (raw extra-cost ct/kWh cached for reference only —
   the live low threshold is recomputed from `sensor.epex_afname_extra` on
   every price evaluation, not read from this cache)
9. ~~`cfg_threshold_high`~~ — no longer set; the high threshold is now a
   fixed constant (0 €/kWh) in *Threshold sanity*
10. `pv_log_buffer`
11. `pv2_present` (true when the PV2 package is detected)
12. `ha_conn_err_window` {start,count} — rate-limit state for *Filter transient HA drops*
13. `hb_last` — time of the last heartbeat publish (group 10)

## Heartbeat (group 10)
*Every 5 s* (group 07, before the enabled/price gate) → link **→ 10 heartbeat** → *Heartbeat (max every 5 min)* → *Publish pv_limiter/version (retained)* node with topic `pv_limiter/heartbeat` (ISO time, retained).
HA: `sensor.pv_limiter_last_run` (MQTT sensor, `device_class: timestamp`) in `pv_limiter_control.yaml`.
Dashboard: "Last run" line under the log title (🟢 ≤ 10 min, 🔴 older, ⏸️ limiter disabled).
Alert: `packages/nodered_heartbeat.yaml` notifies when it is older than 10 min while `input_boolean.pv_limiter` is on, and puts both limits at **100 %** (safe state: no stuck 0 % curtailment while the flow is down).
